correctness.rationale: Forward invariance follows from boundary signs and total conservation. At b=0, d/dt(T-Z-(a/k)log Z)=0 and T<=T0 exp(-at), so a unique positive terminal Z_* solves the monotone final-size equation. Lambert inversion and three elementary W_0 limits prove the sharp vacancy trichotomy. For 0<b<a, e^{bt}E_b(t) has a positive finite limit with explicit exponentially small remaining integral; dominated convergence gives A_b->E_*, and uniform estimates for T,I complete the scaled-time profile. Concavity follows by implicit differentiation. The checked package script executes numerical error-catching tests, not a replacement proof.

value.rationale: The allowed zero-regular-conflict boundary creates a continuous equilibrium family, with initial-data selection governed exactly by vacancy saturation; the result answers which capacity remains unfilled, not merely whether a stable equilibrium exists. The below/at/above-capacity fast-recruitment regimes have sharply distinct inverse-rate, logarithmic/inverse-rate, and exponential signatures. Weak positive conflict produces a noncommuting-time limit and a universal 1/b slow clock, distinguishing eventual population balance from practically observable transients; these are natural structural statistics of the stated model rather than arbitrary cuts.
